clue.text: The only good woman abroad — but she's a dish

parts.note: sole means only, as in a sole survivor
bonne femme is French for good woman, the abroad marking the foreign language

explanation.surface: A grumble that the one decent woman to be found is overseas, with a leering twist that she is attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'She's a dish' plays on the slang for an attractive person; here the dish is a fish course. Sole bonne femme is sole cooked in a white wine and mushroom sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: This French recipe of flatfish poached with mushrooms is a dish served at table.

clue.text: Politician with something of the night?

definitions.text: Politician with something of the night?

parts.words: Politician with something of the night?
parts.note: plays on Ann Widdecombe's famous jibe that Michael Howard had 'something of the night' about him; the night suggests darkness, and an opposition frontbencher is the dark counterpart of a government post

explanation.surface: A sinister politician with a hint of darkness about them.
explanation.walkthrough: In British politics the opposition party names a frontbench team matching the government's ministers; something of the night hints at the dark, shady counterpart of a real office.
explanation.definitionFit: An opposition spokesperson who mirrors a cabinet post is a politician named after a dark outline.

clue.text: It's nothing to put on a pound, giving rise to fat

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the assembled letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: nil means nothing, a score of zero
taken as written
L is the abbreviation for pound, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: A dieter's lament that doing nothing piles on weight and fat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving rise to' turns the whole run NILONAL, which reads upwards as the answer; 'It's' and 'to put' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Wool grease extracted from sheep's fleece is a fatty substance used in ointments.

clue.text: Plan for a pornographic picture?

definitions.meaning: a technical drawing or detailed scheme for building something
read jokingly as a ..., blue meaning smutty and a print being a picture

explanation.surface: Asking whether a design was meant for smut.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a blue film or joke is an obscene one, so a blue print would be a dirty picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A detailed technical drawing is a design or scheme for building something.

clue.text: Postmortem on rise of currency over harvest

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece set over another can enclose it, the outer letters standing on either side
in a down clue, rising means the currency word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the yen is the currency of Japan
crops are what is harvested from the fields

explanation.surface: An inquest into a fall in money set against a poor harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' can mean wrapped around, the reversed currency standing either side of the harvest; 'on' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A necropsy is the medical examination of a dead body, the same as an autopsy.

clue.text: What an apprentice may become, but not at first

definitions.text: What an apprentice may become, but not at first

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for an apprentice is dropped

parts.note: a learner is someone still being trained, like an apprentice

explanation.surface: A trainee will one day be paid, though not right away.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a trainee is not paid well at first but becomes a wage-earner.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee who qualifies goes on to draw a wage, becoming someone paid for work.

clue.text: Old king failing to make the grade

indicators.note: a failing attempt is wrecked, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An old monarch who did not pass the test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' scrambles GRADE; 'to make the' are link words. Edgar was a tenth-century English king.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar the Peaceful ruled England in the tenth century, so he is a monarch of long ago.

clue.text: Game of wits

definitions.meaning: a children's game played with small glass balls
as in losing one's ..., meaning one's sanity

explanation.definitionFit: Small glass balls give the children's pastime, and in idiom they stand for a person's sanity.

clue.text: How a handsome curate may look for interest

definitions.text: How a handsome curate may look
definitions.meaning: split as ..., a fine appearance in clerical robes
a sound placing of money that earns interest

explanation.surface: Admiring how attractive a young clergyman appears in church.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as GOOD IN VESTMENTS, the first sense pictures a good-looking curate in his robes.
explanation.definitionFit: Money placed where it earns a healthy return is a wise financial commitment for interest.

clue.text: A girl has to get her weight right for a job at the Beeb

definitions.note: the definition names a job, while the answer is the person who does it

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
an ounce is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: A woman must watch her weight to land work at the BBC.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beeb is a British nickname for the BBC; 'has to get her' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadcaster who reads the news or introduces programmes fills a familiar BBC post.

clue.text: Actress with nothing to boast about?

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for boast is reversed

parts.note: to brag is to boast
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A performer with no achievements to show off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns BRAG into GARB; 'with' and 'to' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta Garbo was a famous Swedish-born film star of Hollywood's golden age.

clue.text: Poor student transported on the lower deck

indicators.note: transported means carried off elsewhere, so these letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: L stands for learner, a student, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: An impoverished scholar shipped off and stowed below decks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transported' rearranges POOR with L; 'on the' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The orlop is the lowest deck of an old sailing ship, below the gun decks.

clue.text: Scheme of lover somewhat rudely set aside

indicators.note: a scheme rearranges things, so the letters are plotted into a new order
somewhat means only part of the word is used, its tail dropped

explanation.surface: A lover's plan, dismissed rather brusquely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhat' trims RUDELY to RUDE, and 'Scheme of' rearranges LOVER plus RUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A decision that has been overturned by higher authority has been put aside.

clue.text: Uncharacteristic feature of log?

parts.note: a logarithm has two parts: the whole-number part is called the characteristic, so the other part is the one that is not the characteristic

explanation.surface: Something unusual about a log of wood.
explanation.walkthrough: In mathematics a logarithm splits into its whole-number part, the characteristic, and its decimal part; 'uncharacteristic' points to the decimal part.
explanation.definitionFit: In logarithms the decimal fraction following the whole-number characteristic carries this technical name.

clue.text: Location of Seoul once select

definitions.meaning: an old name for Korea, the kingdom whose capital was Seoul
an adjective, as in a select few, meaning picked out

explanation.definitionFit: Joseon was the historical Korean kingdom, and a select group is one picked out.

clue.text: Schooling that's acutely distressing?

definitions.meaning: jokingly, being educated at Harrow, the English public school
deeply upsetting, as of an ordeal

explanation.surface: An education that proves a painful ordeal.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is a famous English private boarding school, so the first sense is a pun: being educated there.
explanation.definitionFit: A harrowing experience is deeply upsetting, and the word also suggests Harrow School education.

clue.text: Golf club refreshment

definitions.meaning: Royal St George's, the Open venue in the Kent town of that name, is often called by the town
a snack of filling between two slices of bread

explanation.definitionFit: A Kent town gives its name to a famous links course, and a filled bread snack is light refreshment.

clue.text: 24 state of untidy chaos

indicators.note: chaos means disorder, so these letters are thrown into a muddle

explanation.surface: A messy, disordered condition.
explanation.walkthrough: '24' points to 24-across, OVERT, so the definition reads as an open, uncovered state; 'chaos' scrambles UNTIDY.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no clothes on is a plainly visible, uncovered condition of the body.

clue.text: Modern technology's at one's fingertips

definitions.meaning: relating to computers and electronic data, read as an adjective
literally relating to the fingers, the digits

explanation.surface: Today's gadgets put everything within easy reach.
explanation.walkthrough: A digit is a finger, so the adjective also means done with the fingers.
explanation.definitionFit: Computer-based technology is described this way, and the word literally refers to fingers.

clue.text: Like many clues in the French game

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other, here inside the French article

parts.note: le is French for the
many crossword clues are across clues

explanation.surface: Comparing crossword clues with a pastime played in France.
explanation.walkthrough: Lacrosse is a team sport played with netted sticks.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a field sport played with long netted sticks and a ball.

clue.text: Leak this with a number for cross-reference

definitions.meaning: a slow escape of liquid through gaps

definitions.text: this with a number for cross-reference
definitions.meaning: read as two words plus a page number, the phrase used in books to direct a reader elsewhere

explanation.definitionFit: Liquid slowly escaping through a gap is a leak, and split in two the word directs readers to a page.

clue.text: Honest journalist produced pulp

parts.note: pure means clean and honest
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A truthful reporter wrote trashy fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulp' looks like cheap fiction from a journalist, but it means mushed food.
explanation.definitionFit: To purée food is to mash it into a smooth pulp.

clue.text: Old emperor is buried in Romberg

indicators.note: one piece is buried inside another, so the letters go into its middle

parts.note: Sigmund Romberg was a composer of operettas

explanation.surface: An ancient emperor's grave lies in a place called Romberg.
explanation.walkthrough: Sigmund Romberg wrote operettas such as The Student Prince; Sigismund was a Holy Roman Emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigismund was a fifteenth-century Holy Roman Emperor, so a ruler from long ago.

clue.text: Leo, the first sign given by a philosopher

indicators.note: the first letter of the word sign is taken

parts.note: A. J. Ayer was a British philosopher

explanation.surface: An astrology column about Leo, the opening star sign, said by a thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: Leo looks like the zodiac sign, but it is Leo Sayer, a British pop singer of the 1970s; 'given by a' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo Sayer is a British pop singer whose first name alone serves as the definition.

clue.text: Public backing to protect a minister

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the assembled letters are reversed
to protect is to surround and guard, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: taken as written
REV is short for Reverend, a minister

explanation.surface: Popular support given to shield a government minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protect' puts the minister inside TO, giving TREVO, which 'backing' then turns round; 'a' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done openly, in public view, is plain and not concealed.

clue.text: Opening of space attempt

definitions.meaning: a way in, such as a doorway into a room

explanation.definitionFit: A doorway is a way in, and a competition submission is an attempt to win.

clue.text: Cancel opening event for being about a minute overdue

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word event is taken
about means going round, so the word for overdue surrounds the other letters

parts.note: late means overdue
I is one, which is a

explanation.surface: An event is called off because it is running a minute late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps LATE round IMIN, splitting it after the L; 'for being' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate something is to remove or get rid of it entirely.

clue.text: 6 felt heart beat for a forebear

indicators.note: to beat something is to batter it, so these letters are knocked into a new order

parts.note: the answer to 6-down, an old English king

explanation.surface: A poignant feeling that one's heart pounded for an ancestor.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' stands for 6-down, EDGAR, and 'beat' rearranges EDGAR with FELT and HEART; 'for' is a link word. Alfred was Edgar's great-grandfather.
explanation.definitionFit: The ninth-century king of Wessex was the great-grandfather of King Edgar, so his ancestor.
